Some people think the title race is already decided, but Joe Hart remains optimistic. While he is paid to be positive, his belief makes sense because Manchester City won the league in 2012 and 2014 by making dramatic late runs. 

When asked about needing to overcome a nine-point deficit, Hart said, "This is how we do things. We like to do it this way. We haven't played as well as we wanted to every week, but the beauty of football is that you get another chance. That starts this Monday against Crystal Palace. We have eight big games left to reach the level we need to be at."

Former rugby star Mils Muliaina has been released from police custody after being arrested on suspicion of sexual assault. The 34-year-old, who played for the New Zealand All Blacks, denies the allegations.

He was arrested last night at Kingsholm Stadium following his team's loss to Gloucester. Muliaina had been playing for Connacht when he was injured and was approached by police. The arrest is related to an incident that happened in Cardiff in March.

QPR players and fans are feeling confident before their important match against Aston Villa this Tuesday. 

Before their big 4-1 win against West Brom last Saturday, QPR had lost 13 of their 14 away games. That win ended a five-game losing streak. QPR is currently in 19th place, only three points away from avoiding relegation.

During the win, coach Chris Ramsey told his players to stay calm. In a press conference on Monday, Ramsey said, "This is a fantastic victory for us. The team's mood is good, and everyone is acting very professional."

Arsene Wenger hasn't decided if he will give Abou Diaby a new contract yet. However, he suggested that the midfielder might stay at Arsenal after this summer. Diaby has struggled with many injuries, playing only 22 games over the last five seasons. He recently returned to play in a practice game on Wednesday. Arsenal plays Liverpool this Saturday, but Wenger likely won't start Diaby in such an important game. He did suggest that Diaby could earn a new contract, possibly one where he only gets paid when he actually plays.

Even without stars like Tiger Woods or Rory McIlroy, the Shell Houston Open in Humble is seeing record-breaking crowds. Because it is the last tournament before the Masters, it is becoming a huge hit. This is thanks to the exciting playing styles of Phil Mickelson and local favorite Jordan Spieth. 

Eighteen months ago, Spieth was criticized for leaving college to join the PGA Tour while he was ranked 809th in the world. Now, at only 21 years old, he has risen to number four. Interestingly, no one is criticizing him anymore.
